term: founded by God through an envoy; agency vocabulary (Confirms, HoldsMandate, FoundedInMandate, CommissionedToTeach)
definition: God founds a society through an envoy when one who holds a mandate from God (HoldsMandate x g: x speaks and acts with authority received from g, without being identified with g) founds it in the exercise of that mandate (FoundedInMandate x g c) and commissions it to teach (CommissionedToTeach x c). Confirms g p is g's confirming the proposition p by a sign that is g's own deed: a testimonial act, not a mere display of power, and not by itself the truth of p. In this sense FoundedAsTeachingAuthority g c, the root's primitive, is satisfied by founding through an envoy as well as by immediate founding. All four agency relations are uninterpreted parameters of the Agency structure; only the premises STMT-RESURRECTION-CONFIRMS-JESUS-MANDATE, STMT-GOD-CONFIRMS-ONLY-TRUTH, STMT-MANDATE-COVERS-JESUS-FOUNDING-WITH-TEACHING and STMT-ENVOY-FOUNDING-IS-GODS-FOUNDING constrain them.
note: Stipulative modeling vocabulary for #357. The mediated sense follows the root's own source, Dei Filius ch. 3 para. 5 (Deus per Filium suum ... Ecclesiam instituit), which describes God's founding as done through the Son; that sentence fixes the sense of the root predicate only and is not used as a premise. A sourced definition would need a source that analyses mission and representation, e.g. Lumen gentium III §§18-20 (already pinned) or Aquinas on mission.
